lesson_title: One Bridge, Three Petrol Stations, Eleven Salons
hook_text: One town, four kinds of market. You shop in all of them every week without knowing their names.
clip_script: One town, four markets. First, forty tables of identical tomatoes — nobody controls the price, and profit invites so many copycats it melts to nothing. Perfect competition. Second, the only bridge over the river. Cross or swim. The bridge picks its toll — high toll, fewer crossings; low toll, more — and because nobody can build a second bridge, its profit lasts forever. Monopoly. Third, three petrol stations on one stretch. Station A raises ten cents? The others don't follow — A stands alone at empty pumps. A cuts ten cents? The others match within the hour, and all three are simply poorer. So the price freezes for months, and the war moves to coffee, loyalty cards and clean forecourts. Oligopoly — a staring contest. Fourth, eleven hair salons, each slightly special: the best braider, the gospel, the late hours. Each can charge a little extra to loyal customers — until her chairs fill, margins fatten, and two new salons open within six months. Profit melts again, but every salon keeps an empty chair some afternoons. Monopolistic competition: slightly wasteful, wonderfully human. Four markets, two dials — how steep the demand, how open the door.
visual_style: A stylised town map that the camera tours: a tomato street, a lone toll bridge, three glowing petrol signs frozen at the same price, and a strip of salons each with one empty chair — with a small slope-dial and door-dial spinning in the corner as each stop is visited.
mood: Curious tour-guide energy with a sly grin at each structure's trick.
pacing: Four brisk stops of roughly equal weight, a snap comparison at the end.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw all four market diagrams from one town map.
